accepted.decision: Add a writer behind --apply and change nothing about the classification. A new pure module src/sync/write.ts turns classifications into planned writes: it filters on isWritable(classification) (never on class alone), computes the content, and computes the owned-view sha to record. The composition root src/commands/sync/index.ts gains applySync(root, version), which reuses the same readManifest + replay evidence, calls planWrites, writes through the existing applyPlan (the only file writer in the codebase, which can create but never delete), then writes the manifest once with an accumulated sync branch. src/sync stays pure and does no fs writes. Content rule, which is load-bearing: a create target is written as produced, verbatim; an append-block target that is absent is written as produced, verbatim; an append-block target that exists is spliced, meaning the produced text between the markers, with filled discovery bodies carried over by the existing preserveDiscovery, is substituted between the present file's own markers and every byte outside them is preserved. The write must NOT go through appendBlock: I measured it on this repository and its withoutSecondH1 step demotes the produced H1 to H2 in both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md, so ownedText(written) stops equalling ownedText(produced) and the next sync reports update forever. The splice satisfies ownedText(written) === ownedText(produced) for both files, which is exactly what makes the second run classify keep. What stays unchanged: classify.ts, ownership.ts, replay.ts, decision 0010's contract, the read-only sync path and its report, the init branch of construct.json, the strategy table and appendBlock (init's first-contact behaviour). A known gap is deferred, not fixed here: replay renders the created-file variant (AGENTS.md.eta, CLAUDE.md.eta) even where init wrote the guest variant (.existing.eta), so applying here replaces CLAUDE.md's thin Construct pointer with the full new-repo block. It cannot be fixed in the writer alone, because comparison and write must use the same produced content, so fixing it means changing what is compared, which is a separate change with its own record. Measured consequences of running --apply on this repository: exactly three paths are written (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, tsconfig.base.json); AGENTS.md changes exactly one line (d4 becomes mikoshi-construct) and all ten discovery bodies survive byte for byte; the drift list loses exactly one entry, tsconfig.base.json, while every other entry keeps its kind; and construct.json here is still the legacy v1 shape, so the write also upgrades it to manifestVersion 3 with the values init recorded unchanged field by field.
accepted.contractChanges: No OpenAPI contract exists; the boundary contract is the CLI surface, the --json shapes and the manifest schema. (1) src/cli.ts: the sync command gains apply: boolean, default false, described as the only way sync writes; its meta description stops saying it writes nothing. No other flag is added and none may override a refusal. (2) Exit codes for sync --apply: 0 when every path classified add or update was written, 2 when a path classified add or update remained unwritten because isWritable refused it (every merge-json target), 1 when there is no construct.json or a write failed; the read-only sync keeps its current 0/1/2 meanings. (3) JSON shape under --apply: the existing syncJson object plus written (array of targets, in write order), pending (array of targets classified add or update that were refused) and ranAt (ISO timestamp); syncJson itself is unchanged. (4) Manifest: no manifestVersion bump. The sync branch already in MANIFEST_VERSION 3 is now populated by a new pure src/manifest.ts export that merges the written paths into manifest.sync.files (accumulating across runs, so an earlier run's recorded path is never dropped) and sets ranAt, fromVersion (manifest.construct), toVersion (running version); it touches no other field. The recorded value per path is ownedSha(target, writtenContent). (5) src/materialize/strategies.ts gains a block substitution export used by the writer; appendBlock keeps its signature and behaviour. (6) Lore gains the apply strings, each with a PLAIN_LORE counterpart, and syncPending and syncMergedNotWritten are reworded so they stop claiming the tool never writes while still stating that no merge-json file is written.
accepted.compositionChanges: architecture/composition/sync.yaml: rewrite description (two entry points sharing one replay: runSync reports, applySync writes only what isWritable allows and records it). Add boundary write with label such as Write - the only files sync writes. Add nodes: apply (label applySync - replay, plan the writes, write, record; path src/commands/sync/index.ts; boundary entry), writes (label planWrites - add and update where isWritable allows, the block spliced, discovery bodies carried over; path src/sync/write.ts; boundary classification), applied (label applyPlan - writes each planned file, creates, never deletes; path src/materialize/apply.ts; boundary write), record (label writeManifest - the sync branch only, the init branch untouched; path src/manifest.ts; boundary write), printApply (label printSyncApply - what was written, what was refused, the exit code; path src/commands/sync/report.ts; boundary report). Change the cli edge into two routes: cli to run labelled report and cli to apply labelled --apply. Add edges: apply to manifest (sequence), classify to writes (route, label --apply), ownership to writes (wires), writes to applied (sequence), applied to record (sequence), record to printApply (sequence). Then run pnpm composition:render so the block in architecture/sync.md is regenerated, and hand-rewrite the prose sections around it: the exit-code section gains the apply codes, and the section titled what this version does not do is replaced by what --apply writes and what it never writes, including the note that a file sync rewrote is still listed as modified by doctor because the baseline is what init wrote and 0006 froze it.
constraints: The writer decides with isWritable(classification) and never with classification.class alone; a table-driven test over the seven classes crossed with the three strategies pins that the written set is exactly add and update crossed with create and append-block.

Write what was compared: for every written append-block path, ownedText(target, written) must equal ownedText(target, produced). Do not route the write through appendBlock; its withoutSecondH1 demotion and its append-when-absent branch are init's first-contact behaviour and were measured to break idempotence on both AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md here.

Never write produced verbatim over an existing append-block file. Substitute only between the present file's own markers, preserve every byte outside them, and carry filled discovery bodies with the existing preserveDiscovery; there is to be no fallback branch that writes the whole produced file over a file that has content outside the block.

Sync never deletes a file, never recreates a path classified removed, never adopts a foreign one, never writes a conflict and never writes a merge-json target, including a package.json whose owned keys make the path update. No flag, env var or option may override any of this, and none is to be added beyond --apply.

construct.json: the init branch is not touched. Only the sync branch is written, it accumulates (a later run must keep an earlier run's recorded paths) and it records exactly the paths written, with ownedSha of what was written. The manifest is written once, after the file writes. When nothing was written, construct.json is not touched at all.

Do not change src/sync/classify.ts, src/sync/ownership.ts, src/sync/replay.ts or decision 0010's contract in this change. Record the deferred variant gap (replay renders the created-file variant even for a block init wrote from .existing.eta) in the new decision record's consequences, and update 0010's Enforced by line where it says the never-deletes rule is L1 review until the writer exists.

src/sync stays pure: no fs writes there. The files are written by the composition root through the existing applyPlan; add no second file-writing primitive. Dependency policy is unchanged (src/sync imports manifest, materialize, presets only, never ui) and the spawn policy in eslint.config.mjs is untouched.

Every new user-facing string lives in src/ui/lore.ts with a PLAIN_LORE counterpart; --plain output for the apply path carries no lore vocabulary and no emoji, asserted the way tests/sync-report.test.ts already asserts it. The apply output lists, per written append-block path, the write effect the classification carries rather than restating it.
A write failure exits 1 with the message through ui.flatline, in the same shape init already uses; it does not leave a half-written manifest, because the manifest is written last.

No dependency is added, no comment or JSDoc is written, tests live in tests/ only, style is fixed with pnpm lint:fix, and no existing test is weakened or skipped. Two live-repository expectations in tests/sync-replay.test.ts flip from update to keep because the ratchet closed; the property they protected (a differing block reads update, not conflict, though discovery filled the markers) stays asserted on constructed inputs in tests/sync-ownership.test.ts, which must not be touched.
After running --apply on this repository, do not hand-edit anything it wrote: that re-creates the drift the list just lost. If a written file fails lint, fix the template and re-apply.

Freeze this repository's current AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md (markers filled, block still at 0.1.0 text) beside tests/fixtures/sync/materialized-by-0.1.0/construct.json under names no tool reads as instructions or lints, and have the apply test copy them into a scratch tree under their real names. Without frozen content the idempotence and marker tests go vacuous the moment the repository itself is written.
acceptance: Running --apply over a scratch tree whose ten discovery markers are filled leaves the body between every construct:discover open and close marker byte for byte identical before and after, asserted once per marker by iterating DISCOVERY_MARKERS rather than by checking the file exists or contains expected text, while the block text outside the markers is proven to have changed to what the templates produce.

A table-driven test pins that planned writes are exactly the paths where isWritable holds: every merge-json target is left untouched, including a package.json whose owned keys make the path update, whose bytes are unchanged and whose path is absent from the manifest's sync.files; and every path classified keep, conflict, removed, orphaned or foreign is compared path by path before and after and is byte-identical.
No file is deleted: the set of files after the apply is a superset of the set before, and the difference is exactly the paths classified add that were written.

Each written path has ownedSha of what was written recorded in construct.json under sync.files, together with a parseable ranAt, fromVersion equal to the manifest's construct and toVersion equal to the running version; a second apply that writes a different path keeps the first path's entry; and a test asserts field by field that every other manifest field (construct, createdAt, preset, ai, review, harness, report, contracts, vars, files key by key, discovery marker by marker) is unchanged, with the legacy-shape normalisation that upgradeManifest already performs named explicitly as the only difference.

--apply over a scratch copy of the frozen 0.1.0 fixture tree followed by a plain sync reports add 0 and update 0, no path recorded but absent (package.json and the other recorded-and-missing paths) is recreated, and a second --apply writes no file and leaves construct.json byte-identical, ranAt included.

construct sync --apply exits 0 when every pending path was written, 2 when a pending path was refused because it is a merge-json target, and 1 without a construct.json; --json --apply emits the report object plus written, pending and ranAt; --plain output carries no lore vocabulary and no emoji.

--apply has been run on this repository and its result is committed: AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, tsconfig.base.json and construct.json. architecture/self-hosting-drift.yaml has the tsconfig.base.json entry removed and the AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and tsconfig.json reasons re-stated to what still differs after the block was written, tests/reproducibility.test.ts is unchanged, and it passes in both directions.

pnpm composition:check passes with architecture/composition/sync.yaml extended and architecture/sync.md regenerated by pnpm composition:render (never hand-edited inside the rendered block), docs/cli.md documents --apply (what it writes, what it never writes, that conflicts are reported and never resolved, that no merged file is written in this version, the exit codes and the doctor-still-calls-it-modified note), and pnpm run quality is green.

brief:
Task: Give `construct sync` its writer, behind `--apply`. Everything it writes and everything it refuses is already decided by the classification in src/sync/ and by decision 0010; this change makes the writing happen and proves it does no harm.

What is written. Paths classified `add` and `update`, and only where `isWritable` says so — which excludes every `merge-json` target, because a three-way comparison is not reconstructible for them from a manifest that predates sync. Do not consult the class alone: `isWritable` exists precisely so a writer reading only the class cannot get it wrong, and a `package.json` whose owned keys make the path `update` must still not be written.

What is never written. `keep`, `conflict`, `removed`, `orphaned` and `foreign`. No file is deleted, no path classified `removed` is recreated, no file the construct never wrote is adopted. There is no flag that overrides any of this and none is to be added.

What is recorded. Each path written gets its owned-view sha recorded in the manifest's `sync` branch, with when the run happened, the version that had materialized the repository and the version that wrote. The `init` branch is not touched: decision 0006 froze it, and a test must assert it field by field before and after, not merely that the file still parses.

The dangerous part, and the reason this task has a condition the others did not. The first real `--apply` will run on this repository, where `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` classify as `update` and hold two days of discovery written into their markers. The only thing standing between that work and a rewrite is the carry-over of the discovery marker bodies. It is the single place in this feature where a mistake costs lost work rather than a revert. So the acceptance is not that the file was written: run `--apply` over a tree whose markers are filled, and compare the body of every discovery marker byte for byte before and after. A test that checks the file exists, or that it contains some expected text, does not cover this.

After the writer runs on this repository, `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` will stop diverging from what the templates produce. `architecture/self-hosting-drift.yaml` declares them as diverging, and the self-hosting test fails in both directions by design — an entry under which nothing differs any more is as much a failure as an undeclared difference. That is the ratchet working. Update the drift list in the same change rather than afterwards, and do not weaken the test.

Idempotence is the proof the writer is honest: `--apply` followed by `sync` must report nothing in `add` or `update`, because the second run compares against what the first one recorded. Prove it on the frozen 0.1.0 fixture rather than by reasoning.

The composition model at architecture/composition/sync.yaml describes the reporting flow; extend it for the writing path and regenerate architecture/sync.md with `pnpm composition:render`, since composition:check runs inside quality. Document `--apply` in docs/cli.md: what it writes, what it will never write, that conflicts are reported and never resolved, and that a merged file is never written in this version.

Repository conventions: no comments in source including JSDoc, every user-facing string lives in src/ui/lore.ts with its PLAIN_LORE counterpart and --plain carries no lore, tests live in tests/ and never beside source, the spawn policy in eslint.config.mjs fails the build if src/ reaches for a child process, a dynamic import, require or createRequire, style is fixed by running lint:fix rather than by hand, no dependency is added, and no existing test is weakened or skipped.

Acceptance criteria so far:
- Running --apply over a tree whose discovery markers are filled leaves the body of every marker byte for byte identical before and after, asserted per marker rather than by checking the file exists or contains expected text; this is the one case where a mistake costs work rather than a revert.
- Paths classified add and update are written only where isWritable allows, so every merge-json target is left untouched including one whose owned keys make the path update, and paths classified keep, conflict, removed, orphaned and foreign leave the tree byte-identical, compared path by path before and after.
- Each written path has its owned-view sha recorded in the manifest's sync branch together with the run time and both versions, while the init branch is byte-identical before and after and a test asserts it field by field.
- --apply on the frozen 0.1.0 fixture followed by a plain sync reports nothing in add or update, no path recorded as removed is recreated, and a conflict is never written and has no flag that would allow it.
- architecture/self-hosting-drift.yaml is updated in this change for the entries that stop diverging once AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are written, with the self-hosting test left unweakened, the composition model extended and architecture/sync.md regenerated, docs/cli.md documenting what --apply writes and never writes, and pnpm run quality green.

The task is classified as high effort; design it before any implementation.
